title: Finite geometric decomposition above a single irreducible component
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $W=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $r:W\to X$ be the projection [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every irreducible component $T\subseteq |X|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], there are finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ of $W$, with $n\geq1$, such that $r^{-1}(T)=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_n$. No connectedness, reducedness, quasi-compactness, or finiteness of the set of irreducible components of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04KZ (lemma-galois-action-irreducible-components-locally-finite-type), assertion (3); Tag 038H (lemma-separably-closed-field-irreducible-components), comparison from a separable closure to its algebraic closure; used together in Tag 04L7 (proposition-units-general), first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Choose $t\in T$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] choose an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ containing $t$, with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Put $V=r^{-1}(U)$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $U\times_k K$ with the pullback of $U\hookrightarrow X$ along $r$; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change, def-weil-open-immersion] identify its underlying space with the open subspace $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], this scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k K)$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ generate $A$ over $k$, then $a_i\otimes1$ generate $A\otimes_k K$ over $K$: every tensor is a finite sum of $a\otimes\lambda$, and writing $a$ as a polynomial in the $a_i$ writes that tensor as the same polynomial in $a_i\otimes1$ with coefficients in $K$. Thus [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] gives finitely many irreducible components of $V$.

source.place: Tag 04KZ (lemma-galois-action-irreducible-components-locally-finite-type), first proof paragraph: finite-type affine chart and Noetherian scalar extension; Schemes Tags 01JY, 01I4 and 01JQ

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of irreducible components $C$ of $W$ contained in $r^{-1}(T)$. By [lem-sfb-field-extension-irreducible-components], $r^{-1}(T)$ is nonempty and is a union of components of $W$, hence equals $\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal S}C$ and $\mathcal S$ is nonempty. For each $C\in\mathcal S$, the same node says that the actual image $r(C)$ is a component of $X$. It is contained in $T$, so maximality gives $r(C)=T$. In particular $t\in r(C)$, and $C\cap V\ne\emptyset$.

source.place: Tags 04KW (lemma-inverse-image-irreducible) and 04KX (lemma-image-irreducible), applied directly to K/k; affine-local finiteness argument for 04KZ(3)

proof.text: For $C\in\mathcal S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] to the open $V\subseteq W$. It makes $C\cap V$ irreducible closed in $V$, with closure $C$ in $W$. It is maximal: if an irreducible closed subset $E$ of $V$ contains $C\cap V$, its corresponding closure in $W$ contains $C$, so maximality of $C$ forces that closure to equal $C$, and the inverse correspondence forces $E=C\cap V$. Thus $C\cap V$ is a component of $V$. Moreover $C\cap V=C'\cap V$ implies $C=C'$ by taking closures. We obtain an injection from $\mathcal S$ into the finite set of components of $V$, so $\mathcal S$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 04KZ, first proof paragraph: a geometric component is determined by its nonempty restriction to an affine chart; Topology Tag 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions), open-subspace correspondence

proof.text: Enumerate the nonempty finite set $\mathcal S$ as $C_1,\ldots,C_n$, with $n\ge1$. Step 2 gives $r^{-1}(T)=\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal S}C=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_n$. This used only one finite-type affine chart meeting $T$; neither $X$ nor $T$ was assumed quasi-compact and no finiteness assumption was made on the other components of $X$. If $X$ is empty there is no $T$, so the universal assertion is vacuous.
